newsitem.title: CHILE: Enersis says it got Brazil's Cerj cheap.
newsitem.headline: Enersis says it got Brazil's Cerj cheap.

text.p: A consortium led by Chilean power investment firm Enersis bought Rio de Janeiro utility Cerj this week at a per-client price well below that of earlier privatizations in Brazil, Enersis General Manager Jose Yuraszeck said.

Enersis spent Friday setting up its management team for Cerj. Enersis headed a consortium which bought 70.2 percent of Cerj Wednesday in a privatization tender and will officially take over on November 28, said Yuraszeck in a statement.
The consortium paid $587 million for Cerj, a price which "in relation to the number of clients served...is significantly less than that paid in previous privatizations in Brazil," said Yuraszeck.

Cerj's price works out to $685 per electricity customer, less than half the $1,478 per client paid for in the privatization of utility Light and $1,116 per client in the sale of another power firm, Escelsa, he said.

Enersis paid even less on a per-client basis for its holdings in Peru and Argentina because of "the lower interest of multinational companies in participating in those privatizations," said Yuraszeck.

Enersis' first concern at Cerj will be to reduce its energy losses, currently running at about 28 percent of total energy produced, an area in which power distribution unit Chilectra has great experience due to high energy loss rates at holdings in Peru and Argentina, said the statement.
At Argentine unit Edesur, energy loss was cut from 26 percent in 1992 to 10.3 percent this year, said Yuraszeck.
